title: Chapter 145 — Managing Delivery Delays
intro: The manufacturer pushed the ship date. The truck broke down. Whatever the reason — the delivery is not happening when promised.

sections.title: Breaking the News
sections.content:
Call, do not email. And call before the customer calls you. 'Hi [name], I am calling about your delivery scheduled for Thursday. Unfortunately, [reason]. I am sorry — I know you were counting on this. Here is what I can do.'

Always call proactively. The customer who discovers the delay by waiting all day for a truck that never comes will never trust you again.

sections.title: What to Offer
sections.content:
Updated timeline with a firm date. Loaner options if available and if the customer is without an essential appliance. Partial credit or accommodation for the inconvenience. Expedited delivery when available — bump them to the next available slot.

The goal is to demonstrate that the delay matters to you as much as it matters to them.

sections.title: Preventing Cascading Loss
sections.content:
A delivery delay can cascade into a lost sale or chargeback if handled poorly. The customer who waits three weeks, gets delayed twice, and never hears from you proactively will cancel the order, buy from a competitor, and leave a devastating review.

Prevent the cascade: communicate early, communicate often, and always have a next step to offer.
